parts:
Austin,

 

Because size is in such different units from aligned Procrustes coordinates, it will dominate any downstream analytics: PCA, MANOVA, etc. So having PC1 explaining 95% and that being size is to be expected (see the size-shape spaces in Mitteroecker et al. 2004).

 

As to your anova question and why your data do not show differences only in species 1, this is challenging to address without more information.  I would suggest some simple plots such as box plots and histograms to visually inspect the patterns among groups. That may assist you in discovering why your intuition about your data is not matching the analytics. Sample sizes may come into play here (and no, RRPP does not alleviate any issues regarding this).

 

As for the test statistic used in pairwise, ‘Dist’ is the correct one. “Var” is for comparing within-group variances = disparity.

 

Dean

Subject: [geomorph-r-package] Testing for centroid size differences amongst different species

 

Hello!

 

So I am wrapping up some analyses looking at how including centroid size as a variable influences species discrimination. I ran my analyses with landmark data in two sets (One with just the landmark coordinates (Procrustes superimposed) and another with the superimposed coordinates and the log centroid size added as another variable. 

 

I ran both data sets through PCA and to no surprise, species lacked clustering with shape exclusive analyses, but when size is added I saw separation between species 1 and all of the remaining species. The first PC explained ~95% of the variation, being centroid size. Based on this, and I know PCA is not a statistical test, I would assume that the only difference between the species I analyzed on the basis of centroid size alone would be between species one and the rest of the species. So in order to test this I ran a ProcD.lm with the following code to evaluate whether centroid size was significantly different amongst the species or not. I expected to find that species one was different from the remaining groups, but instead found that all species differed significantly in centroid size despite this pattern not showing up in the PCA? 

 

#Run  ProcD.lm to test for sig differences in centroid sizes across groups

procA_size<-procD.lm(centroid~species,iter=1000,RRPP=TRUE)

summary(procA_size)

 

#Run pairwise comparison

PW_procA_size<-pairwise(procA_size,groups=species)

summary(PW_procA_size, confidence = 0.95, test.type = "dist")

 

I am working with fossil data, so the design is heavily unbalanced (species observations range anywhere from 2 - 190 specimens per species). I thought that this might be causing the discrepancy, but I am using the RRPP so it shouldn't be. I was also wondering if it could be the test.type I am using for the pairwise summary, should it be var instead of dist? 

 

Sorry for the onslaught of questions, I am so thankful to have this group to refer to for questions!

 

Kindest regards,

Austin
